text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Pager started for KV cache allocator erosion on prod-us-west-2. Continuous-batching rate spiked and fragmentation jumped. Paging oncall @elena

elena: I'm on it. seeing alerts — what do we know about customer impact?

sam: I'm seeing sustained 20-30% drop in serviced QPS for /v1/generate, tail latency 95p -> 2.1s from 400ms. A subset of workers showing repeated cudaMalloc failures in logs.

chris: that smells like arena fragmentation plus cont-batch holding KV refs. I've got allocator stats: free_slots dropping, slabs heavily interleaved. Likely allocator erosion over ~2h window.

marta: any immediate mitigation we can do without a redeploy? customers are pinging SRE.

elena: priority = reduce customer errors. can we throttle batching or force compaction?

sam: we can flip the continuous-batching flag to false per-pool. Doing a quick canary on pool-a: `rbctl set pool-a continuous_batching=false`

sam: canary applied to 3 nodes. monitoring now.

dina: heads-up: disabling continuous batching will increase tokens/sec cost slightly, but reduces KV retention time and should free up capacity.

chris: also trigger one-off arena compaction on healthy nodes: `python infra/tools/arena_compact.py --pool pool-a --mode aggressive` — will iterate and release fragmented slabs. I'll queue compaction for the canary nodes.

sam: can see cont-batch drop, per-node KV cache footprint down ~35% after ~45s on canary. tail latency improving on those nodes.

elena: good. roll to rest of pool? I want two-step: roll canary -> 50% -> 100%.

marta: doing gradual roll now via `rbctl roll pool-a --target 50`.

ryan: FYI CS reports two enterprise customers saw request timeouts around 14:10 and 14:17; they didn't lose data but experienced degraded latency. They're asking for timeline and mitigation plan.

elena: note for postmortem: include affected customer ids and SLA risk. For now we have rollback plan if compaction harms throughput.

chris: compaction completed on canary nodes, no regressions. Proceeding to 50% rollout of continuous_batching=false and compaction.

sam: roll to 50% done. cluster-level errors dropping from 3.9% -> 0.8%. tail latency 95p trending down to ~550ms.

dina: starting to see evictions in KV logs during compaction window as freed slabs are reclaimed — expected.

elena: nice. hold at 50% for 10m to confirm. If stable, we make this global hotfix and open a follow-up to revert after allocator patch.

chris: investigating root cause: allocator metadata growth correlated with a specific batching config change rolled out 6h earlier. There's a pattern where small micro-batches cause high slot churn and slab aging. Candidate fix: change slab sizing and add cross-pool compaction sweep and a protective fallback for libcudamalloc OOMs.

sam: I captured a sample stack trace from one OOM: ```
RuntimeError: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
  at torch/csrc/.../alloc.cpp:345
  at kv_store/cache.cc:872
  at batching/continuous_batcher.cc:204
```

chris: thanks. I'll prototype an allocator hotpatch: reduce per-request KV reservation, bias small allocations toward a separate small-object arena, and add a GC sweep when fragmentation ratio > 0.7.

marta: ops checklist: 1) wide disable of cont-batching (done), 2) compaction run (done), 3) monitor & notify customers (in progress), 4) push hotfix patch for allocator (next).

ryan: I'll send an interim note to the affected accounts: "We've applied mitigations to reduce latency and errors; engineering is tracking root cause and will follow up with timeline for permanent fix." Want to include any technical detail?

elena: keep it high level: mention fragmentation and batching interplay, we've applied a temporary config change, a permanent patch is being developed.

chris: ETA for hotfix branch and canary build ~2 hours. If tests pass we'll stage to canary nodes then roll. Hotfix will include: allocator GC sweep, small-object arena, safer cudaMalloc fallback path.

sam: I'll prepare monitoring dashboards to watch fragmentation ratio, cont-batch queue lengths, and cudaMalloc failures. Slack alert thresholds adjusted.

elena: excellent. summary for pager: initial cause likely regression in batching config increasing allocator churn -> fragmentation -> cuda OOMs on heavy workloads. Mitigation: disabled continuous batching cluster-wide (gradual), ran compaction sweeps, monitoring. Next steps: allocator hotfix, postmortem, customer comms.

pagerbot: incident status updated to "Mitigated" by elena. Incident ID #INC-2023-2387. Please continue followups in #incidents or open a tracking ticket.

marta: moving to mitigation->postmortem state. Assigning owners: chris (root cause & patch), sam (deploy & monitoring), ryan (customer comms), elena (incident lead).

elena: thanks team. I'll keep the thread open until hotfix is in canary and stable.
